text:
Pellham Borough Council voted 19 to 6 on Thursday evening to approve a new harbour levy, ending months of debate over how to fund upkeep of the town's quays and dredging works.

The vote took place on 14 March 2024 at the council's regular evening session, and is recorded in the certified minutes of that meeting, which list the 19 to 6 roll-call result.

The levy sets a charge of 2.4% on commercial mooring and cargo-handling fees. It is projected to raise £1.8 million over five years.

Councillor Odette Varnham, chair of the Pellham Harbour Committee, moved the motion. "This levy gives the harbour a stable footing," she said. "Those who use it commercially will help keep it working."

The levy applies to commercial operators only.
